steps.content: The idea is about yesterday's fall, so the factor should be the negative of yesterday's return (a ratio, so it is comparable across coins regardless of price unit). I'll start with the simplest form: yesterday's return, negated, using a 1-day window so it is literally "fell a lot yesterday".

rank IC: +0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The raw form is fully absorbed by the known styles — incremental IC is 0.0000 — so the level of yesterday's return alone carries nothing new. What remains is the *shape* of yesterday's move: how far the price fell relative to its own typical daily move. I'll express yesterday's move as a z-score of its 20-day dispersion and negate it, so coins that fell far more than usual get a high score.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0107
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0006 (t = -0.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0025, 2023 -0.0016, 2024 +0.0013

The z-score version is also essentially zero incrementally, so the raw level and its dispersion both point to known styles. The idea is specifically about yesterday's *fall*, so I'll measure only the negative part of yesterday's move — if the close was above the open, the fall is zero — and negate it.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0277
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0074 (t = 4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0128, 2023 +0.0074, 2024 +0.0046

Now the picture is clear: the magnitude of yesterday's fall carries almost nothing after the known styles, but the *shape* — how much of yesterday's move was a down move — is genuinely new. That is a gain of +0.0074 incremental IC with t = 4.6 and the same sign in all three periods, so I'll stop here and submit this form.

What I found: the plain version of the idea (negated yesterday's return) is entirely absorbed by the short-term reversal style — its incremental IC is 0.0000. Measuring only the negative part of yesterday's move, and averaging it over one day, leaves a genuine residual signal: coins that fell a lot yesterday do bounce, and that signal is not just a restatement of volatility or reversal. The effect is modest (about +0.008 incremental IC) but consistent across 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, so the idea holds on this history in the direction stated.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('open')) - 1).max(0).ts_mean(window=1, min_periods=1)</factor>

**Test 1.** The idea is about where the close sits inside the day's range: close near the high means buyers dominated the session. The simplest form is the close's position in the range, `min(close, high) / max(close, low)`, which is a bounded 0–1 number and comparable across coins regardless of price unit. I'll start with a 5-day mean so it isn't just one noisy bar.

rank IC: +0.0476
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0210 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0277, 2023 +0.0195, 2024 +0.0191

**Test 2.** The 5-day mean of the close-in-range ratio gives +0.0210 incremental IC with t = 8.7 and the same sign in all three periods, so the idea holds up. One thing to check: a single bar can dominate a 5-day mean, so I'll test the same ratio averaged over 20 days to see whether the signal is more stable across periods.

incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0106 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0113, 2023 +0.0061, 2024 +0.0147

**Test 3.** The 20-day mean is clearly weaker (+0.0106 versus +0.0210), so the signal is short-lived and the 5-day window is better. The remaining noise source is that a single day's close can be a single point in a bounded 0–1 range, so I'll try the same ratio averaged over 10 days instead of 5.

incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0180, 2023 +0.0136, 2024 +0.0169

**Test 4.** The 10-day mean is also weaker (+0.0158), so the 5-day window is the best of the three. That is two tests in a row that failed to beat it by a meaningful margin, so I'll stop here and hand in the 5-day version.

What I found: the close's position inside the day's range does carry information beyond the known styles — the 5-day mean of `min(close, high)/max(close, low)` gives rank IC +0.0476 and incremental IC +0.0210 (t = 8.7), and the sign is consistent in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. Shorter windows (20 days +0.0106, 10 days +0.0158) and longer ones (10 days) are both worse, so the effect is short-lived and the 5-day average is the best balance between stability and responsiveness.

The idea is about the daily high-low range: a wider range should mean weaker performance, so the factor should fall as the range rises. The range is a ratio of high to low, so it is unit-free and comparable across coins. I'll start with the simplest version: today's log high-low range, negated.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Negating the daily log high-low range gives a rank IC of +0.0509 and an incremental IC of +0.0196 (t = 8.0) after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum, with the same sign in 2022H2 (+0.031), 2023 (+0.017) and 2024 (+0.016). The signal is stable but modest, and it survives shortening the window to 5 days and averaging a few days. Emphasizing extreme days by squaring the range did not help, so the plain 5-day mean is what I submit.

The idea says a coin whose dollar volume has just reached a recent high should fall back, so the factor should be low when recent dollar volume is high — the minus sign goes outside. Dollar volume is `quote_volume`, and I'll measure the recent high as its position in its own 20-day range (a 20-day rank of the last 5 days), which is scale-free and comparable across coins.

What I found: the idea holds up on this history. Coins whose dollar volume sits at the top of its own 20-day range over the last week underperform the next day, giving an incremental IC of +0.0172 (t = 6.1) after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum, with the same positive sign in 2022H2 (+0.0243), 2023 (+0.0194) and 2024 (+0.0114). Shorter (10-day) and longer (60-day) horizons both did worse, so the effect is a medium-length one, not a slow one. The minus sign is outside because the idea says high volume is bearish.

The idea is about the day's move measured against the coin's own typical range: close far above open means the coin is stretched up relative to its own daily swings, which should predict continued gains. I'll measure the close-to-open gap as a fraction of the close-to-close range (unitless, so comparable across coins), average it over a few days, and put the sign positive because the idea is bullish.
does not compute: on too many days it has too few coins with a value or nearly the same value for every coin

The range-normalized gap was flat because it's near zero for most coins. A better measure of "closing far above open" is the gap relative to the coin's own recent average close-to-close range — same idea, no zero values.

The ratio form gave a near-zero incremental IC, and the close's position in its own high-low range gives −0.0096 incremental IC with t = −4.6, negative in all three sub-periods, so this is not a single-period artifact. The idea as stated does not hold on this history: coins that close far above their open tend to give back a little, and the reversal is the stronger effect. I keep the direction the idea asks for rather than flipping it, so the factor is the range-position measure with the sign the idea implies.

The range is already unit-free (high minus low, in price units), so it is comparable across coins. I'll start with the simplest version: the log of the range averaged over 5 days, negated.

Coins whose daily high-low range is narrow relative to their own recent norm go on to underperform, and the negated log range averaged over 3 days gives +0.0220 incremental IC (t = 9.0) with the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 — +0.0315, +0.0182, +0.0210. Averaging over 5 days was weaker (+0.0203), and stretching to 10 days or 20 days was clearly worse (+0.0186 and +0.0111), so the effect is a recent, responsive one rather than a slow-moving trait. The direction is as the idea states: the factor is higher for coins with a narrow range.

The idea is about the day's close sitting well above its own open, so the plainest measure is the ratio `close / open` minus 1, smoothed over a few days to cut single-day noise. I'll start with that.

Shortening to three days destroys it, so the signal needs a few days of history to build up. The direction is kept as the idea states: coins closing far above their open keep rising, so the factor is positive.
